title: Still-free variables avoid the clause's literals
statement: Fix a number $n$ of variables, and let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on them. Suppose the free literals of a clause are given as a list, each literal paired with its position index, and let a decision-tree path be a list of variable–direction pairs whose length is at least the number of literals. Running the clause-processing operation on this list, this path, $\rho_0$, and $\sigma$ returns an updated restriction $\rho_0'$ in place of $\rho_0$. If a variable $v$ is free under $\rho_0$ and remains free under $\rho_0'$, then no literal on the list has $v$ as its underlying variable.
hypotheses_covered: ρ₀ and σ are restrictions on n variables
the clause's literals form a list, each tagged with its position index
the path is a list of variable–direction pairs
the number of literals is at most the path length
v remains free under the updated restriction ρ₀' returned by the operation
replaced:
Contrapositive of $\rho_0$-stability: if $\rho_0\,v = \mathrm{none}$, the
\texttt{SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits} output keeps $\rho_0$ unset at $v$, and there
are at least as many path entries as literals, then no input literal has variable $v$.
